blocks.text: Spanish has 27 letters. The combinations ch and ll used to count as separate letters but no longer do. Spanish spelling is very regular: once you know the rules, you can read any word aloud.

blocks.title: Spain vs Latin America
blocks.text: In Spain the letters v and w are called uve and uve doble. Latin America often says ve and doble ve. To spell a name: C-A-R-L-O-S = ce, a, erre, ele, o, ese.

blocks.title: Tips for Dutch speakers
bullets: Keep each vowel short and pure. In many Dutch accents the long ee and oo glide a little (zee, boot). Spanish e and o never glide.
Say every vowel clearly, also when it is unstressed: ca-sa, not ca-suh. Spanish has no weak “schwa” sound.

blocks.text: Every Spanish word has one stressed syllable. Two simple rules tell you which one, and a written accent marks every exception.

blocks.title: What an accent does and does not do
blocks.text: A written accent only shows where to stress the word. It never changes the sound of the vowel. Words stressed on the third-to-last syllable always carry one: teléfono, música, sábado.

Strong vowels are a, e, o. Weak vowels are i, u. Two strong vowels are two syllables (le-o). A strong and a weak vowel, or two weak vowels, form one syllable: bue-no, tiem-po, ciu-dad. An accent on the weak vowel splits them: dí-a, pa-ís.

items: Question words always carry an accent, in questions and exclamations: qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cómo, cuánto, cuál (¡Qué bien!).
Opening marks: questions start with ¿ and exclamations with ¡, as well as ending with ? and !
Lower case: days, months, languages and nationalities have no capital: lunes, enero, español, holandés.
Titles capitalise only the first word: Cien años de soledad.
Double letters are rare: mostly ll and rr (and sometimes cc or nn). Never double a vowel the way Dutch does: hablar, not hablaar.

blocks.title: Free vocabulary: Dutch endings that match Spanish
bullets: Dutch -tie = Spanish -ción: natie / nación, informatie / información, situatie / situación.
Dutch -teit = Spanish -dad: universiteit / universidad, activiteit / actividad.
Dutch -logie = Spanish -logía: biologie / biología, tecnologie / tecnología.

rows: Stress is on the third-to-last syllable, so it needs a written accent.
Ends in n, so the rule says stress the second-to-last syllable. The stress is on the last, so it takes an accent.
Questions open with ¿ and the question word carries an accent.
tú (you) has an accent; tu (your) does not.
Languages are written in lower case.
The k sound before e or i is spelled qu.
A hard g before e or i needs a silent u: gue, gui.
